name: Smuggling: desync detect -> cache poison -> reset capture
goal: Prove front/back desync, convert it into cache poisoning, and land poisoned password-reset links to capture victim tokens.
preconditions: A front proxy paired with a backend that disagrees on CL/TE framing.
impact: Cache-wide content injection and account takeover of arbitrary reset recipients.

steps.purpose: Prove the CL.TE desync differential with a deterministic timing oracle.
steps.on_success: Craft poison-prefix requests; step 3 scales it.

steps.purpose: The reverse differential — one of the two usually fires.
steps.on_fail: Both silent -> H2 desync / client-side desync are documented gaps (need h2/browser tooling); fall back to header-based poisoning (step 3 without desync).

steps.purpose: Scale: poison cacheable responses with attacker content via unkeyed headers (works with or without desync).
steps.on_success: Poisoned cache serves payload to every visitor of that path.
steps.on_fail: Header filtered -> find other unkeyed inputs via param-miner; CRLF (web/CRLF response-header injection) to inject whole headers.

steps.purpose: Victim-targeted capture: reset emails carry attacker-host links when the Host header is unkeyed.
steps.on_success: Capture reset tokens -> account takeover; pair with cache poison for self-reset via admin page (PortSwigger combo).
steps.on_fail: Host pinned -> X-Forwarded-Host alternates (X-HTTP-Host-Override etc.), or poisoning path for stored variant.

entry_points: any cacheable path behind a proxy

recon.name: Framing differential timing
recon.how: CL.TE and TE.CL timing pairs on likely-cached and likely-uncached paths.
recon.signal: Consistent delay on one framing = desync direction.

recon.name: Duplicate-header acceptance
recon.how: Send duplicate Content-Length and Transfer-Encoding mixes; error messages and 400/501 responses fingerprint the front.
recon.signal: Front rejects one shape, origin accepts another.

recon.name: Cache-key mapping
recon.how: Cache-buster param + candidate unkeyed headers; diff cached vs uncached responses.

recon.name: Reset-link host audit
recon.how: Trigger a reset and read the link's host; then vary X-Forwarded-Host shapes.
recon.signal: Email link host changes with header.

recon.name: Peer stack clustering
recon.how: Favicon hash + header clustering finds sibling apps on the same edge — one desync often repeats across the fleet.

variants: H2.CL / H2.TE desync (needs h2 tooling — documented gap)
dorks: shodan: favicon-hash + Via/Server clustering to find identical front/back stacks
pivot_hints: poisoned admin cache + reset combo (PortSwigger classic)
pair with cache-deception-pii for data theft
document desync alone — it is critical by itself
